experiment: E091 read by hand: hand classification of E083 treatment queries as need statements
rubric:
Rubric written before viewing any results or search data:
  served:    query explicitly asks how to fix, resolve, troubleshoot, or obtain a working guide for a specific fault code or technical problem
  partially_served: query asks about the meaning/definition of a code/error but does not explicitly ask for a resolution guide
  unserved:  query is generic, boilerplate, or not clearly a need statement

Chrome words removed before classification: error, code, codes, fault, alarm, troubleshooting, meaning, what, does, how, the, for, and, with, manual, guide, messages
Sequence counters stripped from query text before evaluation

Specific domain terms used to distinguish genuine need from generic chrome: boeing, airbus, cockpit, avionics, hydraulic, pneumatic, engine, landing gear, electrical, flight control
classifier_version: hand-classification by author using rubric written before viewing results; reads only query_text field, no search results, no scrape data

comparison_e090.experiment: E088 / E090 discrimination test on known labels
comparison_e090.observation: The 'read by hand' step on query text (E091) produces a different served fraction than the classifier on search results (E090). This is expected and desirable per STATE.md §263: classifying the need statement itself, before any classifier is written, should yield different (and more accurate) evidence. The classify_served instrument on search results has 4/5 false positives on known-unserved (E090 G1 FAIL), so a different distribution when reading the query text by hand is the point — it provides independent ground truth not subject to the classifier's false positives.

discrimination_test_status: NOT APPLICABLE — E091 provides 'labels known by construction' per STATE.md §265, independent of the classify_served instrument. A discrimination test would need a different instrument design, not the classify_served / Bing search + keywords class.
labels_known_by_construction: 14 served, 4 partially_served, 17 unserved across 35 E083 treatment queries, classified from query text alone using a rubric written before viewing results. These hand classifications are 'known by construction' per STATE.md §265 and can serve as ground truth for future instrument design, independent of the classify_served / Bing search + keywords class which has been shown to fail discrimination testing (E088, E090).
next_action_per_STATED_md: STATE.md §265: Discrimination test must pass before population measurement. Since the current instrument class (classify_served / Bing search + keywords) fails on both automated labels (E088) and hand-classified labels (E090), a new instrument design is required. Per STATE.md §263: the 'read by hand' step has now been taken — need statements classified from query text by hand provide independent labels known by construction. Per STATE.md §267: the next session must not start from classify_served over Bing in an eighth domain. The concrete opportunity E088 leaves open — whether fault/error-code domains hold unserved needs — can now be addressed by building an instrument informed by the E091 hand-classified ground truth, rather than by another screen of the same broken classifier.
next_experiment_planned: E092 — Design and run a discrimination test using E091 hand-classified labels as ground truth, with a simplified or redesigned instrument (not classify_served / Bing + keywords). This would test whether a different instrument can pass the G1 discrimination gate (served(unserved) <= 0.30 with CI lower > 0) on these labels, providing the 'instrument that has first passed a discrimination test on labels known by construction' that STATE.md §265 requires before population measurement.
